c.h: To fully immerse yourself in EVE Online select fullscreen mode. Fullscreen increases performance on some computers as well.
Resizes your game client to the resolution indicated. In windowed mode, regardless of your physical screen resolution, the aspect ratio of the game will always be correct.

Adjusting the UI scaling allows you to make the entire UI larger or smaller. This is particularly helpful if you're playing EVE on your TV, or if you really need that bit of extra space on a small screen, but it may reduce the visual quality of the UI.
If you have multiple graphics cards in your computer you can switch between them here
Vertical refresh sync, or V-Sync, locks the FPS to the monitors refresh rate
Upscaling renders the game in a lower resolution and uses an algorithm to reconstruct the frame at a correct resolution
Changing the upscaling setting may affect game performance and graphic quality
Increases framerate at the cost of slightly decreased image quality in fast-paced situations

sections.t: These settings allow you to tweak performance and quality of the rendering

c.h: Disabling may improve performance, especially when using depth effects or HDR

Post Processing includes bloom effects and other full screen effects. The cost of enabling post processing is only dependent on your display resolution and not on the number of objects in the 3D scene, i.e., the performance impact will not grow with scene complexity.
Changing shader quality might impact the performance of the game greatly
Changing texture quality might impact the performance of the game greatly, especially when you have a graphics card with low video memory
Changing the level of detail quality influences performance, especially on older graphics cards
Shadows require more video memory and will impact performance on lower-end hardware
Changing the ambient occlusion quality influences performance, especially on older graphics cards
Changing the volumetric effects quality influences performance, especially on older graphics cards

Disabled - No dynamic reflections (Low Shader Quality Only)

Low - Background, planet and hangar reflections

Medium - Station and Structure reflections (and the above)

High - Reflections from selected visual effects (like explosions) (and the above)

Ultra - Lens flare reflections (and the above). Reflections are updated more frequently
Adjust the graphics brightness for space and ship hangars

Each ship in EVE Online can hold multiple turrets and missile launchers. Turning off animations for these can help FPS in massive fleet combat scenes but usually doesn't change performance under normal circumstances. This change takes effect on the next session change or log in.
Various explosions and lighting effects can be disabled for performance debugging circumstances
Various explosions and lighting effects can be disabled for performance debugging circumstances
Turning off explosions might have a positive impact on the client performance during fleet engagements but will generally not make a big difference during normal gameplay

Turning off drone models might have a positive impact on the client performance during fleet engagements but will generally not make a big difference during normal gameplay. This change takes effect on the next session change or login.
Disabling trails can have a positive impact on game performance, especially during fleet fights
Disabling GPU particles can save some memory and improve performance, but some effects such as missile trails will no longer be visible
Disabling asteroid environments can have a positive impact on game performance around asteroids and asteroid belts
Disabling inspace skinning effects can have a positive impact on performance. Skinned ships will still be visible but changes while in space will be disabled
Simulates camera lens, out of focus regions seem blurry
Uses a simpler, less visually pleasing manner for displaying characters in the character creation. Only advisable for lower end machines.
Turns the background in the character creation and re-customization, as well as the character preview window, green in order to allow players to easily remove background from screenshots
Changing texture quality might impact the performance of the game greatly, especially when you have a graphics card with low video memory
Affects the sensitivity of camera motion, except for zooming
Affects the inertia of all camera motion such as zooming, orbiting, and panning
Offsets the camera's center to the left or right
Toggle the camera shaking when warping and when your ship is hit
Toggle idle camera movement on/off
Reverses the zoom direction for the camera when using the scroll wheel or left+right mouse buttons
Applies the camera offset to the user interface. This affects the default positions of windows and shifts centered messages and pop-up boxes towards your ship.
Enables automated camera movement based on ship velocity, zoom level, and events such as docking and undocking
Flips the control for the camera in the vertical axis

Enables compact mode by default in all windows that can be compacted. You can always manually override the compact mode per-window via the window controls even when this is enabled.
When enabled, UI highlight color palette is mapped to exclude problematic hues. A client restart is required for changes to take full effect.

c.desc:
Opt-in feature preview for a work-in-progress redesigned in-space ship HUD:

• Updated medallion for hitpoint, capacitor, speed, and heat display
• New module status display and animations for improved feedback and clarity
• Redesigned utility button column and safety toggle
• More prominent module overloading controls with clearer state changes and damage display

Toggle the preview version on or off at any time, no restart required.
Currently only applies to ship HUDs, structure control HUDs remain unchanged at this time.
Additional features will continue to be added over time, and player feedback from the feature preview will be used to improve future versions.
